mechanism.basis: Q = h·A·(T_surface – T_coolant); with T_surface ≈ 700°C and T_coolant moving 293K→273K, the fractional change in ΔT is only (700–273)/(700–293) = 1.06, i.e., ~6% increase in heat flux — far short of the 30–50% surface finish improvement claimed.

physics_of_phenomenon.basis: 0°C is not cryogenic (NIST definition: < –150°C); SS304 and Ti-6Al-4V show <2% change in E and <5% change in α between 20°C and 0°C (per standard ASME/ASM materials handbooks), so σ = E·α·ΔT in the workpiece is effectively unchanged.

evidence.basis: Only one cited record (doi:10.3390/jmmp6060128), and its title indicates it studies machining parameter optimization generally, not a controlled A/B test isolating coolant temperature as the independent variable.

prior_art.basis: doi:10.1016/0043-1648(73)90228-7 (1973) and doi:10.1115/imece2013-63777 already teach surface-finish dependence on cutting environment/dielectric; the specific 0°C coolant variant is incremental, not novel.

experiment_design.basis: n=10/group gives limited power against the high-variance confounder of progressive tool wear; no specification of fresh-tool-per-sample or randomized block design means tool wear can dominate the Ra signal and produce either false positive or false negative.

boundary_conditions.basis: Ti-6Al-4V k≈7 W/m·K (low) and SS304 k≈16 W/m·K (higher); low-k materials concentrate heat at the tool-workpiece interface, so coolant temperature has LARGER effect on low-k materials, inverting the stated boundary condition.

predicted_effect_quantification.basis: Typical turning Ra CV is 10–20%; published cooling-environment studies (doi:10.3390/ma19091850) show Ra improvements <15% from cooling changes alone, contradicting the lower bound of the 30–50% claim.

reproducibility_translation.basis: Water-based coolant at 0°C in an open bath during sustained turning will (i) absorb heat from chips and rise above 0°C within minutes (water cp = 4.18 kJ/kg·K; a single cut can release kJ-scale energy), (ii) risk freezing/icing at the workpiece-fixture interface, and (iii) splash onto machine ways causing corrosion — none of which is addressed in the experimental specification.

final_objection: KILLED.
